title: A Morning on a Texas Ranch
description: Step into a Texas cattle-ranch scene with longhorns, riding tack, ropes, and livestock terms.
cardDescription: Step into a Texas cattle-ranch scene with longhorns, riding tack, ropes, and livestock terms.
subtheme: A Morning on a Texas Ranch
focus: This scene uses cattle and ranch-equipment words associated with Texas ranching. Many are used elsewhere too; the longhorn gives the puzzle a particular regional connection.
solvingTip: Distinguish an animal or herd from the riding equipment and the tools used to handle livestock. Direct definitions explain the working terms.

Enclosure used to hold or handle ranch animals
Looped rope used to catch or handle livestock

Property devoted chiefly to raising livestock on a large area

Group of cattle kept or moving together

Grass-covered land where ranch livestock graze
Barrier marking or enclosing a ranch field

answerNotes.LONGHORN: Texas Longhorn cattle are known for their horns. The breed connection gives this ranch scene a specific Texas reference.
answerNotes.CORRAL: A corral is an enclosure for handling animals. A pasture is grazing land and need not have the same purpose or size.
answerNotes.LARIAT: A lariat is a rope used with a loop. The word names equipment rather than a rider's title.
answerNotes.BRAND: A livestock brand identifies ownership. The clue uses the ranching sense rather than a product's trade name.
answerNotes.STEER: A steer is a male animal with a specific husbandry status. It is not the same term as a bull.

title: Texas Wildflowers in Spring
description: Follow a Texas spring roadside through bluebonnets, other wildflowers, and the parts that help a bloom grow.
cardDescription: Follow a Texas spring roadside through bluebonnets, other wildflowers, and the parts that help a bloom grow.
focus: The Texas connection begins with bluebonnets and regional wildflower names. Some flower terms are common across the country, while direct clues introduce less familiar names.
solvingTip: Start with a plant part or season word. Use crossings for a longer flower name rather than needing to recognize it at first glance.
words: Texas wildflower named for its blue bonnet-shaped blossoms
Plant group that includes Texas bluebonnets
Showy wildflower whose name also describes a painter's tool
Daisy-family wildflower also commonly called tickseed
Five-letter flower name for plants with clusters of blooms
Walking route beside which wildflowers may be seen
Plant structure from which a new wildflower can grow
One colored segment surrounding a flower's center
Supporting stalk beneath a wildflower's bloom
An open flower, or the act of flowering
Season associated with many Texas bluebonnet displays
Plant part anchoring a wildflower below ground

answerNotes.BLUEBONNET: Bluebonnets are lupines and are closely associated with Texas spring landscapes. Flower color can vary even though blue is their familiar color.
answerNotes.LUPINE: Bluebonnets belong to the lupine group. The clue asks for the broader plant name rather than one local flower name.
answerNotes.PAINTBRUSH: Indian paintbrush is a familiar wildflower name in Texas and other regions. The puzzle uses the shorter common-name element PAINTBRUSH.
answerNotes.COREOPSIS: Coreopsis is a flowering plant group. Tickseed is another common name; neither term means the flower is an insect.
answerNotes.PRIMROSE: Evening primrose is a common name used for plants distinct from true primroses. The clue explicitly asks for the missing part of that name.

title: Pecan Pie at the Texas Table
description: Gather pecans, pastry, and familiar baking tools around a Texas-associated dessert table.
cardDescription: Gather pecans, pastry, and familiar baking tools around a Texas-associated dessert table.
subtheme: Pecan Pie at the Texas Table
focus: The pecan is Texas’s state tree, and pecan pie connects that local reference with familiar kitchen words. The clues describe ingredients and objects rather than giving a baking recipe.
solvingTip: Look for the nut, its outer covering, the pastry, or a kitchen item. A word can name a container here rather than an ingredient.
words: Edible nut produced by Texas's state tree
Edible inner part of a shelled pecan
Pastry shell forming the base and sides of a pie
Cylindrical kitchen tool used to flatten pastry, with spaces omitted
Written list of ingredients and preparation instructions
Baked pastry dish with a filling such as pecans
Hard outer covering cracked to reach a nut's edible part
Food category that includes pecans in everyday kitchen language
Single wedge cut from a round pie
Unbaked flour mixture rolled out for a pastry base
Protective garment worn over clothes while preparing food
Metal baking container, as in pie ___
Enclosed heated appliance used for baking a pie
Sweet ingredient often used in a dessert filling

answerNotes.PECAN: The pecan is Texas's state tree. Its edible kernel is inside the shell; the nut and the tree share the same name.
answerNotes.KERNEL: The kernel is the part used as food. The shell is the protective covering around it.
answerNotes.CRUST: A pie crust supports or encloses the filling. It is different from the hard shell that protected the nut.
answerNotes.ROLLINGPIN: Rolling pin is two words in ordinary writing. Its letters form one continuous answer in the grid.
answerNotes.RECIPE: A recipe gives amounts and instructions. These clues identify kitchen vocabulary and are not themselves a tested recipe.

title: An Evening at a Texas Dance Hall
description: Hear fiddles and accordions while exploring the country two-step and other social-dance words.
cardDescription: Hear fiddles and accordions while exploring the country two-step and other social-dance words.
subtheme: An Evening at a Texas Dance Hall
focus: This dance-hall scene brings together the country two-step, instruments, and social dances heard in Texas. It does not require knowing a recording date, musician biography, or song lyric.
solvingTip: Separate an instrument from a dance, a movement, and a musical quality. Several short body-position words help cross longer answers.

Pattern of beats and accents guiding dance steps

answerNotes.TWOSTEP: The country two-step is associated with Texas dance halls as well as other places. Different dances also use the name two-step, so the clue specifies the country setting.
answerNotes.FIDDLE: A fiddle and a violin are the same kind of instrument. The term fiddle often signals a musical tradition or playing style.
answerNotes.ACCORDION: An accordion produces sound using air moved by bellows. It appears in several dance traditions, including those heard in Texas.
answerNotes.POLKA: Polka reached Texas through immigrant dance traditions, among others. A dance-hall program need not be limited to one style.
answerNotes.TEMPO: Tempo describes speed. Rhythm describes the arrangement of sounds and accents over time.

title: A Road Trip Across Texas
description: Travel between Texas cities, a national park, and a historic mission using direct geographic clues.
cardDescription: Travel between Texas cities, a national park, and a historic mission using direct geographic clues.
focus: This Texas route includes named places and map features rather than a real driving itinerary. The clues give clear location hints, and some place names omit their spaces in the grid.
solvingTip: Start with a city or landmark you recognize. A short map or road word can provide crossings for a longer geographic name.

answerNotes.AUSTIN: Austin is Texas's capital. Houston and Dallas are larger but do not hold that role.
answerNotes.ALAMO: The Alamo is in San Antonio. The clue identifies a historic site, not a modern state capital.
answerNotes.RIOGRANDE: The Rio Grande forms much of the international boundary beside Texas. It does not form the entire boundary between the United States and Mexico.
answerNotes.BIGBEND: Big Bend National Park takes its name from a great bend in the river. The place name is written as two words outside the grid.
answerNotes.PANHANDLE: The Texas Panhandle is the state's northern projecting region. The same descriptive word is also used for regions in other states.
